body.purpose: The log entry at the foot of the plate. The only prose on the page and the largest type on it. Capped at 62ch.

label.purpose: Identifier, locale pair, readout cells, channel row. Everything that is not the log.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out. The one easing in the system; the chassis powers on, it does not bounce.

motion.name: chassis-draw
motion.purpose: The plate and its frame draw left to right on load; the frame trails by 100ms.

motion.name: decode
motion.purpose: Readout cells resolve out of the field's glyph alphabet after the plate draws.

motion.name: log-in
motion.purpose: The log lands last in the power-on sequence.

motion.name: scramble
motion.purpose: One-shot decode on link hover and focus.

components.name: Link
components.description: Every link on the site. One global selector, no opt-in class; hover inverts to a solid signal block.
components.css: .ds-link { position: relative; display: inline-block; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; letter-spacing: 0.13em; padding: 0.25em 0.45em; margin: -0.25em -0.45em; white-space: pre; text-shadow: 0 0 6px #0a0a0a, 0 0 14px #0a0a0a, 0 0 22px #0a0a0a; } .ds-link:hover, .ds-link:focus-visible { background: #0000ff; color: #fff; text-shadow: none; outline: none; }

components.name: Link (current page)
components.description: Marked with aria-current="page"; a 1px underline at 0.4em offset.
components.css: .ds-link-current { display: inline-block; color: #fff; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 0.4em; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; letter-spacing: 0.13em; padding: 0.25em 0.45em; white-space: pre; }

components.name: Readout Band
components.description: The instrument band. Label and value differ by tone only, never by size. Flush against the plate below it.
components.css: .ds-band { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 2.5rem; padding: 0.55rem 0.85rem; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.15); border-bottom: none; background: #0a0a0a; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; letter-spacing: 0.13em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-cell { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 0.5em; } .ds-cell i { font-style: normal; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.68); } .ds-cell b { font-weight: 400; color: #fff; white-space: pre; }

components.name: Observation Plate
components.description: The signature container: a 1px frame with four L-shaped registration ticks set 9px inside the corners.
components.css: .ds-plate { position: relative; height: 180px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.15); background: #0a0a0a; overflow: hidden; } .ds-tick { position: absolute; width: 13px; height: 13px; } .ds-tl { top: 9px; left: 9px; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); } .ds-tr { top: 9px; right: 9px; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); border-right: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); } .ds-bl { bottom: 9px; left: 9px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); } .ds-br { bottom: 9px; right: 9px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); border-right: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.55); }

components.name: Log Entry
components.description: The only prose on the page. Anchored bottom-left inside the plate, capped at 62ch, with a single short scrim stop.
components.html:
I'm Alex, a full-stack developer. Six years turning product ideas into things people actually use.

Brussels, soon.
components.css: .ds-log { max-width: 62ch; color: #fff; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.95; letter-spacing: 0.035em; text-shadow: 0 0 10px #0a0a0a; } .ds-log p { margin: 0 0 1.5em; text-wrap: pretty; } .ds-log p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }

components.name: Crosshair Reading
components.description: The probe's numeric output, landing in a fixed cell in the channel row rather than floating beside the cursor.
components.css: .ds-vector { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 0.5em; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; letter-spacing: 0.13em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-vector i { font-style: normal; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.68); } .ds-vector i + b { margin-right: 0.85em; } .ds-vector b { font-weight: 400; color: #fff; white-space: pre; }

narrative.overview:
The site presents itself as an instrument, and the thing it observes is its own generative field. Everything on screen is either the phenomenon or the apparatus around it: an identifier plate, a band of live readouts, a framed observation window with registration ticks, a crosshair probe, and a channel row. The person is the log entry at the foot of the plate — the largest type on the page, and the only thing on it written by a human.

The register is precise rather than loud. There is one typeface, one hue, one rule weight, and no corner is ever rounded. Density and tone do all the work that color and size normally do. What makes it feel made rather than templated is that the instrument is not decorative — the numbers are real, read off the running simulation and the browser, and the field genuinely dims itself underneath type instead of the type wearing a glow to survive.

The confirmed anti-reference is the arrangement this replaced: a centered paragraph floating on an edge-to-edge canvas. A generative background with no edge is wallpaper; giving the field a frame is what turns it into an artifact under measurement.
keyCharacteristics: One monospace voice at two sizes; hierarchy from tone and position, not scale steps
Zero radius anywhere; hairline rules at a single weight
A single hue, reserved for state
Live values only — nothing on the chassis is authored
Depth carried by a wide grey ramp, never by shadow

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: #0000ff is reserved for state. If an element is not being hovered, focused, or selected, it is greyscale.

rules.name: The Wide Band Rule
rules.body: The field's ramp must span from near-ground to near-white. A narrow band of midtones is what makes a generative field read flat — every cell lands in the same tonal register regardless of what the simulation is doing. Depth is a range problem, not a brightness problem.

rules.name: The Marks-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: mark is for ticks and hairlines only. Any tone that carries text starts at dim and is verified against the ground.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: The system has exactly two type sizes: the log and everything else. New elements pick one; they do not introduce a third. Hierarchy is built from tone, position, and spacing.

rules.name: The Fixed Footprint Rule
rules.body: Any element whose text changes at runtime sets white-space: pre and pads to a stable width, so no live value can reflow the row it sits in.

rules.name: The Decode Rule
rules.body: Text that resolves on load resolves out of the field's own glyph alphabet, left to right, rerolling on a ~45ms tick rather than every frame. A faster reroll reads as noise instead of a decode.

rules.name: The Subtract, Don't Stack Rule
rules.body: At narrow widths the chassis sheds cells; it never wraps a band onto two rows or reorders the four bands.

rules.name: The Field Recedes Rule
rules.body: Type never wears a glow to survive the field. The field dims itself underneath the type. This is also the mechanism that holds text contrast — the field's bright end reaches #c0c0c0, which would fail against white type without it.

rules.name: The Cut, Not Moulded Rule
rules.body: Instruments are cut. No corner is rounded, no border exceeds 1px, and no element gets a second border weight to signal importance.

dos: Do measure every value shown on the chassis. Read it off the running field or the browser; if it cannot be measured, it does not appear.
Do give any new region an edge. A generative surface without a frame is wallpaper.
Do mark new foreground text with data-field-shadow so the field recedes beneath it.
Do keep new elements at one of the two existing type sizes.
Do set white-space: pre on anything whose text changes at runtime.
Do orchestrate motion as one power-on sequence — plate draws, readouts decode, log lands — rather than giving each new component its own entrance.
donts: Don't add a radius, a second border weight, or a shadow.
Don't introduce a second hue, or use #0000ff anywhere but hover, focus, and selection.
Don't let an interface element draw from the field's grey ramp.
Don't raise the field's ambient floor to add texture; ambient lifts every cell into one tone and erases the voids the currents are read against.
Don't set a fixed particle floor. Traces scale to the grid (~1 per 30 cells); a fixed floor saturates a phone-sized grid into a solid block.
Don't restore a multi-stop text-shadow scrim. The attenuation mask is the contrast mechanism.
